- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots the true decline; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for each subsequent day after a spike.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model should not forecast further decline; instead, expect a rebound within 3–5 days.
- Sentiment history with repeated negative values (e.g., -0.22, -0.61) should trigger a “sentiment-weighted dampening” — reduce forecast magnitude by 10–15% if sentiment is persistently negative.
- For horizon > 10 days, model tends to underestimate true volatility; increase forecast variance by 5–10% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
